runtime_mode: upstream mock adapter; discovery only; not native CAD evidence

tools.name: open_model
tools.title: Open Model
tools.description:
Open a SolidWorks model (part, assembly, or drawing).

Opens an existing SolidWorks file and makes it the active document for further
operations. Supports all standard SolidWorks file formats and provides detailed model
information upon successful opening.

file_path.description: Full path to the SolidWorks file (.sldprt, .sldasm, .slddrw)

tools.name: create_part
tools.title: Create Part
tools.description:
Create a new SolidWorks part document.

Creates a new SolidWorks part document from ``template`` (a .prtdot path) or,
without one, the default part template. The new part becomes the active document
and is ready for modeling operations such as sketch creation and feature addition.

template.description: Part template (.prtdot) path; omit to use the SolidWorks default

tools.name: create_assembly
tools.title: Create Assembly
tools.description:
Create a new SolidWorks assembly document.

Creates a new SolidWorks assembly document from ``template`` (a .asmdot path) or,
without one, the default assembly template. The new assembly becomes the active
document and is ready for component insertion, mating, and assembly-level operations.

template.description: Assembly template (.asmdot) path; omit to use the SolidWorks default

tools.name: create_drawing
tools.title: Create Drawing
tools.description:
Create a new SolidWorks drawing document.

This tool creates a new drawing document from ``template`` (a .drwdot path) or,
without one, the default drawing template. The new drawing will become the active
document.

template.description: Drawing template (.drwdot) path; omit to use the SolidWorks default

tools.name: close_model
tools.title: Close Model
tools.description:
Close the current SolidWorks model.

Closes the currently active SolidWorks document with an option to save changes before
closing. This is essential for proper model lifecycle management and preventing data
loss.

tools.name: create_extrusion
tools.title: Create Extrusion
tools.description:
Create an extrusion feature from the active sketch.

Creates a 3D extrusion feature (boss or cut) from the currently active 2D sketch.
Supports advanced options like draft angles, thin features, bidirectional extrusion, and
various end conditions for professional modeling workflows.

thin_thickness.description: Thickness for thin wall feature in mm

tools.name: create_revolve
tools.title: Create Revolve
tools.description:
Create a revolve feature from the active sketch.

Creates a 3D revolve feature by rotating the active 2D sketch profile around a specified
axis of revolution. Supports full and partial revolves, thin features, and bidirectional
revolution for comprehensive rotational modeling.

thin_thickness.description: Thickness for thin wall feature in mm

tools.name: get_dimension
tools.title: Get Dimension
tools.description:
Get the value of a dimension from the current model.

Retrieves the current value of a named dimension from the active SolidWorks model.
Dimensions can be from sketches, features, or global dimensions. Useful for parametric
modeling and design validation.

tools.name: set_dimension
tools.title: Set Dimension
tools.description:
Set the value of a dimension in the current model.

This tool modifies the value of a named dimension and rebuilds the model. Use this to
parametrically modify your model dimensions.

tools.name: set_units
tools.title: Set Units
tools.description:
Set the active document's linear unit system.

Accepts ``mm``, ``cm``, ``m``, ``in`` or ``ft`` (plus common aliases
such as ``inch`` or ``millimeters``). The setting is applied and then
read back from the document; if the readback disagrees the tool
reports an error rather than a false success.

unit_system.description: Linear unit system: mm, cm, m, in, or ft

tools.name: create_cut_extrude
tools.title: Create Cut Extrude
tools.description:
Cut material from a sketch profile in the active model.

Creates a Cut-Extrude feature (Insert > Cut > Extrude). Use this after
exit_sketch when you want to remove material — e.g. to create windows,
holes, slots, or any through/blind cut in an existing solid body.

Sketch selection is never a silent guess: pass ``sketch_name``
explicitly whenever you're not certain which sketch this should act
on (e.g. more than one sketch could be unconsumed, or other tool
calls ran in between). If omitted, only the sketch most recently
created/exited in this same session is used, and only when it still
exists in the model — there is no further fallback. Any ambiguity or
mismatch is reported back as an error naming the sketch(es) actually
found in the model, rather than cutting the wrong profile.

Direction: a one-way cut (Blind or ThroughAll) goes along the sketch
plane's normal. From a sketch on a face, or on a plane that touches
the body only on one side (e.g. a Top Plane sketch under a block
extruded up from it), that can point away from the material. The
tool then cuts the other way and returns
``cut_extrude.direction_flipped: true``, so you don't need to guess
``reverse_direction``. For a sketch on a plane through the middle of
the body, use ``ThroughAllBoth`` (or ``ThroughAll`` with
``both_directions``) to cut both sides.

input_data.description:
Depth, direction, draft, and
optional sketch_name parameters.

reverse_direction.description: Cut against the sketch normal instead of along it. Usually not needed: if the requested direction finds no material, the cut is retried the other way and the reply sets direction_flipped

end_condition.description: 'Blind' (cut 'depth' mm), 'ThroughAll' (through the body, one way) or 'ThroughAllBoth' (through the body both ways, for a sketch inside the body)

both_directions.description: With end_condition 'ThroughAll', cut through the body both ways (same as 'ThroughAllBoth')

sketch_name.description: Sketch to cut from, e.g. 'Sketch3'. If omitted, the sketch most recently created/exited in this session is used, but only if it still exists in the model — there is no other fallback. Pass this explicitly whenever more than one unconsumed sketch could exist, or after any operation that might have changed the active sketch.

tools.name: add_fillet
tools.title: Add Fillet
tools.description:
Add a fillet (rounded edge) to selected edges of the current model.

Rounds the specified named edges with the given radius. Edge names use the
SolidWorks convention, e.g. 'Edge<1>', or you can leave edge_names empty to
fillet all edges if the adapter supports it.

edge_names.description: Edges (or faces) to fillet. Accepts a topology name (e.g. 'Edge<1>'), a coordinate hint in metres ('x,y,z') to select the nearest edge, or 'face:x,y,z' to select a whole face — which fillets every edge bounding it in one call. Prefer 'face:' over a coordinate on an edge that sits exactly on a shared boundary between two faces (e.g. a hole rim flush with a flat face): the nearest-edge match there can silently resolve to a different, unrelated edge. Leave empty to use whatever is *currently selected* in the live SolidWorks UI (e.g. entities read back via get_selected_entities and left selected) without touching the selection — this is the most reliable option when the user has hand-picked specific edges, since it never round-trips through coordinates. Falls back to filleting all edges only if nothing at all is selected.

tools.name: add_chamfer
tools.title: Add Chamfer
tools.description:
Add an equal-distance chamfer to selected edges of the current model.

Chamfers the specified named edges with the given distance. Edge names use
the SolidWorks convention, e.g. 'Edge<1>', or you can leave edge_names empty
to chamfer all edges if the adapter supports it.

edge_names.description: Edges (or faces) to chamfer. Accepts a topology name (e.g. 'Edge<1>'), a coordinate hint in metres ('x,y,z') to select the nearest edge, or 'face:x,y,z' to select a whole face — which chamfers every edge bounding it in one call. Prefer 'face:' over a coordinate on an edge that sits exactly on a shared boundary between two faces (e.g. a hole rim flush with a flat face): the nearest-edge match there can silently resolve to a different, unrelated edge. Leave empty to use whatever is *currently selected* in the live SolidWorks UI (e.g. entities read back via get_selected_entities and left selected) without touching the selection — this is the most reliable option when the user has hand-picked specific edges, since it never round-trips through coordinates. Falls back to chamfering all edges only if nothing at all is selected.

tools.name: create_sweep
tools.title: Create Sweep
tools.description:
Sweep the active profile sketch along a named path sketch.

Creates a swept boss/protrusion (Insert > Boss/Base > Sweep). Requires
two sketches in the active part: a closed profile sketch and an open
path sketch named by ``path``. The profile is inferred as the sketch
that is not the path (in the usual "draw profile, draw path, sweep"
flow this is unambiguous). Optionally applies a constant twist along
the path.

path.description: Name or ID of the sweep path

tools.name: create_loft
tools.title: Create Loft
tools.description:
Loft a solid between two or more profile sketches.

Creates a lofted boss/protrusion (Insert > Boss/Base > Loft) blending
the listed profile sketches in order. Each profile must be a closed
contour. Optional guide curves shape the transition between profiles.

input_data.description:
Profile names, optional guide curves,
and tangency/merge options.

profiles.description: List of profile names or IDs

guide_curves.description: List of guide curve names or IDs

tools.name: insert_component
tools.title: Insert Component
tools.description:
Insert a part or sub-assembly into the active assembly.

Call ``create_assembly`` first. Position is in millimetres from the
assembly origin.

**The component file must contain solid geometry** — SolidWorks
silently refuses to insert an empty part, so a missing or empty
component surfaces as an error rather than a fabricated success.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the .sldprt or .sldasm to insert

tools.name: add_mate
tools.title: Add Mate
tools.description:
Mate two components in the active assembly.

Positions components relative to one another — coincident planes to
stack or align them, concentric to line up axes, distance to hold a
gap.

Entities are selected by feature name, so only each component's
reference planes and axes can be mated. Mating to a specific face or
edge needs entity names this adapter cannot enumerate.

component_a.description: First component instance name, as reported by list_components

entity_a.description: Named feature on the first component. Only tree features (reference planes and axes) can be selected

entity_b.description: Named feature on the second component

mate_type.description: coincident, concentric, perpendicular, parallel, tangent, distance or angle

distance.description: Distance in millimetres, for a distance mate

angle.description: Angle in degrees, for an angle mate

tools.name: list_components
tools.title: List Components
tools.description: List the top-level components of the active assembly.

tools.name: delete_feature
tools.title: Delete Feature
tools.description:
Delete a feature or sketch from the active model.

Deleting a parent feature also removes everything that depends on it —
SolidWorks' normal cascade — so the response lists every feature that
went, not just the one named.

name.description: Feature or sketch name, e.g. 'Boss-Extrude1' or 'Sketch1'

tools.name: suppress_feature
tools.title: Suppress Feature
tools.description:
Suppress or unsuppress a feature in the active model.

Suppressing rolls a feature and its children out of the model without
deleting it — the reversible way to turn off a feature that is causing
trouble.

suppress.description: True to suppress, False to unsuppress

tools.name: rename_feature
tools.title: Rename Feature
tools.description:
Rename a feature on the feature tree.

SolidWorks silently refuses a rename onto a name another feature
already uses, so the new name is read back and a mismatch is reported
as an error rather than a quiet success. Renaming a feature to its
current name is a no-op success.

input_data.description: The feature and its new name.

tools.name: select_feature
tools.title: Select Feature
tools.description:
Select a named feature, sketch, plane or component.

Replaces the current selection by default; pass ``append: true`` to
add to it (e.g. to select several features in turn). A name that
cannot be selected is an error, never a quiet success.

input_data.description: The feature name and append flag.

feature_name.description: Feature, sketch, plane or component name, e.g. 'Boss-Extrude1', 'Sketch1', 'Front Plane' (an '@Part1' suffix is ok)

append.description: Add to the current selection instead of replacing it

tools.name: select_face_edges
tools.title: Select Face Edges
tools.description:
Select every edge of one face of the active part (multi-select).

Identify the face with exactly one of ``point`` (a point on it, mm),
``side`` (``top``/``bottom``/``front``/``back``/``right``/``left`` or
``+X``..``-Z``; top=+Y, front=+Z, right=+X as in SolidWorks' default
views - the furthest flat face facing that way) or ``plane`` (a
reference plane name - the body face lying on it). ``edge_type``
narrows to ``linear`` or ``circular`` edges (e.g. hole rims).

The edges become the live SolidWorks selection, so the next
``add_chamfer`` / ``add_fillet`` call with an empty ``edge_names``
acts on exactly them. Anything that changes the selection in between
(including the user clicking in SolidWorks) changes what is used.

input_data.description:
Face identifier, edge filter and
append flag.

point.description: A point on the face, [x, y, z] in mm

side.description: Outward direction of the face: +X/-X/+Y/-Y/+Z/-Z or right/left/top/bottom/front/back (top=+Y, front=+Z, right=+X, as in SolidWorks' default views); picks the furthest flat face that way

plane.description: Reference plane name, e.g. 'Front Plane'; picks the body face(s) lying on it

append.description: Add to the current selection instead of replacing it

tools.name: rebuild_model
tools.title: Rebuild Model
tools.description:
Force a rebuild of the active model and report what is wrong.

Use after programmatic edits (``set_dimension``, feature edits) to
confirm the model rebuilds cleanly. When features fail, the response
is an error whose ``data.errors`` names each failing feature with its
SolidWorks error code, the features/sketches it depends on, and a
concrete ``hint`` for fixing it. Warnings alone still succeed.

anyOf.description:
Input schema for forcing a model rebuild.

Attributes:
    top_level_only (bool): Rebuild only the top level of an assembly.

top_level_only.description: Rebuild only the top level of an assembly (default: full rebuild including sub-assemblies)

input_data.description:
``top_level_only`` for
assemblies; omit for a full rebuild.

tools.name: undo
tools.title: Undo
tools.description:
Undo the last operations in the active model.

SolidWorks accepts an undo with nothing left to undo without
complaining, so the response reports whether the feature tree actually
changed rather than assuming it did.

anyOf.description:
Input schema for undoing model operations.

Attributes:
    count (int): Number of operations to undo.

tools.name: create_reference_plane
tools.title: Create Reference Plane
tools.description:
Create a reference plane offset from an existing plane or planar face.

Adds a new plane to the feature tree, parallel to and offset from the
named reference. The returned plane name can be passed straight to
``create_sketch`` to sketch anywhere other than the six built-in
planes.

Angled planes are not supported by this tool: an angled plane needs a
second reference (an axis or edge) to rotate about, which this
signature cannot take. Use ``offset`` for parallel planes. An
``offset`` of zero is rejected — a plane coincident with its
reference is not useful.

input_data.description:
Reference name, offset,
angle and flip.

reference.description: Name of the reference plane or planar face to offset from, e.g. 'Front Plane'

offset.description: Offset distance in millimetres. Must be non-zero — a plane coincident with its reference is not useful

angle.description: Angle in degrees. Not yet supported: an angled plane needs a second reference this tool cannot take, so a non-zero value errors. Use offset for parallel planes

tools.name: create_axis
tools.title: Create Axis
tools.description:
Create a reference axis along a principal direction.

Builds an axis from the intersection of two built-in planes: x from
Top + Front, y from Front + Right, z from Top + Right.

reference.description: Principal axis direction: 'x', 'y' or 'z' (case-insensitive; a leading +/- is stripped)

tools.name: create_reference_point
tools.title: Create Reference Point
tools.description:
Create a reference point on the active part.

Two modes:

- ``along_curve`` — a point on the edge under ``(x, y, z)`` mm, placed
  ``distance`` mm from the edge start, or at ``percent`` (0–100) of
  its length. Give exactly one of ``distance`` / ``percent``.
- ``face_center`` — a point at the centroid of the face under
  ``(x, y, z)`` mm.

The coordinate must lie on the target edge/face; SolidWorks resolves
it with a coordinate pick. ``InsertReferencePoint`` always returns a
feature, so success is confirmed by the feature tree growing.

input_data.description:
Mode, coordinate, and the
along-curve parameter.

mode.description: 'along_curve' (a point on an edge) or 'face_center' (the centroid of a face)

x.description: X of a point on the target edge/face, in mm

y.description: Y of a point on the target edge/face, in mm

z.description: Z of a point on the target edge/face, in mm

distance.description: along_curve only: offset from the edge start in mm (give exactly one of distance or percent)

percent.description: along_curve only: position as 0-100 of the edge length

tools.name: mirror_feature
tools.title: Mirror Feature
tools.description:
Mirror solid bodies or features about a plane.

Selects the named sources and the mirror plane, then mirrors them.
The mirror is verified by comparing model volume before and after:
SolidWorks can report a feature even when it mirrored nothing, so a
volume that did not grow is reported as an error rather than a
false success.

input_data.description:
Source names, mirror plane, and
merge/mirror_bodies flags.

features.description: Body or feature names to mirror. At least one required. For a body mirror these are the names as they appear under Solid Bodies, which for a lofted wing is the loft's own name

mirror_plane.description: Plane name to mirror about, e.g. 'Right Plane'

merge.description: Merge the mirrored result with the original body

mirror_bodies.description: Mirror whole solid bodies rather than individual features. Defaults to True, which is what works for anything built from a loft or sweep - a feature mirror only resolves when the feature's own sketch sits on the mirror plane

tools.name: pattern_circular
tools.title: Pattern Circular
tools.description:
Pattern features around an axis.

Selects the named axis and features, then creates a circular
pattern. The pattern is verified by comparing model volume before
and after: SolidWorks can report a feature even when it patterned
nothing, so a volume that did not grow is reported as an error
rather than a false success.

input_data.description:
Feature names, axis, count,
angle, and equal_spacing.

features.description: Names of the features to pattern. At least one required.

axis.description: Name of the axis to rotate about, e.g. 'Axis1' as created by create_axis

count.description: Total number of instances including the original. Must be at least 2 - a pattern of one is just the original feature

angle.description: Total angle in degrees to spread the instances over. Defaults to a full 360

tools.name: create_sketch
tools.title: Create Sketch
tools.description:
Create a new sketch on the specified plane.

Creates a new sketch on a reference plane and enters sketch edit mode. This is the first
step for creating any 2D geometry that will be used for 3D features like extrusions,
revolves, or sweeps.

tools.name: add_line
tools.title: Add Line
tools.description:
Add a line to the current sketch.

Adds a line segment between two points in the active sketch. Lines are fundamental
sketch entities used for creating profiles, construction geometry, and complex shapes.

x1.description: Start point X coordinate in mm

y1.description: Start point Y coordinate in mm

x2.description: End point X coordinate in mm

y2.description: End point Y coordinate in mm

tools.name: add_circle
tools.title: Add Circle
tools.description: Add a circle to the current sketch.

center_x.description: Circle center X coordinate in mm

center_y.description: Circle center Y coordinate in mm

tools.name: add_rectangle
tools.title: Add Rectangle
tools.description:
Add a rectangle to the current sketch.

Creates a rectangular profile defined by two opposite corner points, automatically
generating four connected line segments forming a closed rectangle suitable for
extrusion or other 3D operations.

x1.description: First corner X coordinate in mm

y1.description: First corner Y coordinate in mm

x2.description: Opposite corner X coordinate in mm

y2.description: Opposite corner Y coordinate in mm

tools.name: exit_sketch
tools.title: Exit Sketch
tools.description:
Exit sketch editing mode.

Exits the current sketch editing mode and returns to the 3D modeling environment. This
is required after completing sketch geometry before creating 3D features like
extrusions, revolves, or sweeps.

tools.name: check_sketch_fully_defined
tools.title: Check Sketch Fully Defined
tools.description: Check whether a sketch is fully defined.

anyOf.description:
Input schema for checking sketch definition status.

Attributes:
    sketch_name (str | None): Optional sketch name to inspect.

sketch_name.description: Optional sketch name. If omitted, checks the active or last sketch.

tools.name: add_arc
tools.title: Add Arc
tools.description:
Add an arc to the current sketch.

Creates a circular arc defined by center point, start point, and end point. Arcs are
essential for creating rounded corners, curved transitions, and complex curved profiles
in mechanical designs.

center_x.description: Arc center X coordinate in mm

center_y.description: Arc center Y coordinate in mm

start_x.description: Arc start point X coordinate in mm

start_y.description: Arc start point Y coordinate in mm

end_x.description: Arc end point X coordinate in mm

end_y.description: Arc end point Y coordinate in mm

tools.name: add_spline
tools.title: Add Spline
tools.description:
Add a spline curve to the current sketch.

Creates a smooth, free-form spline curve that passes through or near the specified
control points. Splines are ideal for creating organic shapes, complex profiles, and
smooth transitions in industrial design.

points.description: List of spline control points with x, y coordinates

tools.name: add_centerline
tools.title: Add Centerline
tools.description:
Add a centerline to the current sketch.

Creates a construction/reference line that serves as a centerline for symmetrical
features, revolution axes, or construction geometry. Centerlines are non-geometric
entities used for reference only.

x1.description: Start point X coordinate in mm

y1.description: Start point Y coordinate in mm

x2.description: End point X coordinate in mm

y2.description: End point Y coordinate in mm

tools.name: add_polygon
tools.title: Add Polygon
tools.description:
Add a regular polygon to the current sketch.

Creates a regular polygon with specified number of sides, center point, and
circumscribed radius. Polygons are useful for creating hexagonal nuts, octagonal
features, and other multi-sided geometric shapes.

tools.name: add_ellipse
tools.title: Add Ellipse
tools.description:
Add an ellipse to the current sketch.

Creates an elliptical entity with specified center and major/minor axes. Ellipses are
useful for creating oval holes, ergonomic profiles, and complex curved features in
mechanical and industrial design.

tools.name: add_sketch_constraint
tools.title: Add Sketch Constraint
tools.description:
Add a geometric constraint/relation between sketch entities.

Creates geometric relationships between sketch entities such as parallel, perpendicular,
tangent, coincident, etc. Essential for creating fully defined, parametric sketches that
maintain design intent.

entity2.description: Second entity name or ID (if required)

entity3.description: Third entity ID. Required for 'symmetric' (the centerline of symmetry); must be null for all other relations.

relation_type.description: Relation type (parallel, perpendicular, tangent, coincident, etc.)

tools.name: add_sketch_dimension
tools.title: Add Sketch Dimension
tools.description:
Add a dimension to sketch entities.

Creates dimensional constraints that control the size of sketch entities. Dimensions are
essential for creating precise, parametric designs that can be easily modified and
maintain manufacturing tolerances.

In live SolidWorks automation, sketch dimensions can otherwise trigger the interactive
``Modify`` approval dialog. The adapter suppresses the relevant sketch-input preferences
for the automation session and uses the dedicated radial/diameter APIs for circles and
arcs so this tool remains non-interactive.

entity2.description: Second entity name or ID (for distance dimensions)

value.description: Dimension value in mm or degrees

tools.name: sketch_linear_pattern
tools.title: Sketch Linear Pattern
tools.description:
Create a linear pattern of sketch entities.

Generates a linear array of selected sketch entities in specified direction(s) with
defined spacing and count. Essential for creating hole patterns, vent grilles, and
repetitive geometric features.

tools.name: sketch_circular_pattern
tools.title: Sketch Circular Pattern
tools.description:
Create a circular pattern of sketch entities around the sketch origin.

Generates a circular array of selected sketch entities. The
rotation axis is always the **sketch origin** — SOLIDWORKS'
``CreateCircularSketchStepAndRepeat`` does not expose a
pattern-centre parameter. Position the seed entity at the
desired radius from the origin; the pattern derives its radius
from the seed's centre.

Essential for creating bolt circles, gear teeth, and other
radially symmetric features around the sketch origin.

tools.name: sketch_mirror
tools.title: Sketch Mirror
tools.description:
Mirror sketch entities about a centerline.

Creates mirrored copies of selected sketch entities about a reference centerline,
maintaining symmetrical design relationships. Essential for creating symmetric parts and
reducing modeling time.

tools.name: sketch_offset
tools.title: Sketch Offset
tools.description:
Create an offset of sketch entities.

Generates offset copies of selected sketch entities at a specified distance, maintaining
the original entity shape while creating parallel geometry. Essential for wall
thickness, machining allowances, and clearance features.

tools.name: sketch_tutorial_simple_hole
tools.title: Sketch Tutorial Simple Hole
tools.description:
Tutorial: Create a simple circular hole sketch.

Demonstrates complete workflow for creating a basic hole sketch that can be used for
through-holes, counterbores, or other circular features. This tutorial shows the
fundamental sketch-to-feature process.

tools.name: tutorial_simple_hole
tools.title: Tutorial Simple Hole
tools.description:
Create a simple hole as a guided tutorial workflow.

Builds a sketch circle on the selected plane, exits the sketch, and creates a cut
feature using the supplied diameter and depth. Useful as an end-to-end example of a
basic subtractive feature.

center_x.description: Hole center X coordinate in mm

center_y.description: Hole center Y coordinate in mm

depth.description: Hole depth in mm (None for through hole)

tools.name: create_drawing_view
tools.title: Create Drawing View
tools.description:
Create a drawing view of a SolidWorks model.

Creates technical drawing views including orthographic projections, isometric views,
section views, and detail views from 3D models. Essential for generating production
drawings and technical documentation.

model_path.description: Path to the SolidWorks model file

view_type.description: Type of view (orthographic, isometric, section, detail)

tools.name: add_dimension
tools.title: Add Dimension
tools.description:
Add a dimension to the current drawing.

Creates dimensional annotations on drawing views including linear, radial, angular, and
diameter dimensions. Essential for manufacturing specifications and quality control
documentation.

dimension_type.description: Type of dimension (linear, radial, angular, diameter)

entity1.description: First entity to dimension (edge, face, point)

tools.name: add_note
tools.title: Add Note
tools.description:
Add a note or annotation to the current drawing.

Creates text annotations, callouts, and notes on drawings for specifications,
instructions, and additional manufacturing information. Essential for comprehensive
technical documentation.

leader_attachment.description: Entity to attach leader line to

tools.name: create_section_view
tools.title: Create Section View
tools.description:
Create a section view of the current drawing.

Generates section views that show internal features by cutting through the part along a
specified section line. Essential for revealing hidden geometry, internal structures,
and complex assemblies.

section_line_start.description: Start point of section line as [x, y]

section_line_end.description: End point of section line as [x, y]

tools.name: create_detail_view
tools.title: Create Detail View
tools.description:
Create a detail view of a specific area.

Generates magnified detail views of specific regions to show fine features, tight
tolerances, and intricate geometry that requires enhanced visibility for manufacturing
and inspection.

tools.name: update_sheet_format
tools.title: Update Sheet Format
tools.description:
Update the sheet format and title block information.

Applies drawing templates and updates title block fields with project information,
revision data, and drawing metadata. Essential for standardized documentation and
drawing control.

sheet_size.description: Sheet size (A4, A3, A2, A1, A0)

tools.name: auto_dimension_view
tools.title: Auto Dimension View
tools.description:
Automatically dimension a drawing view.

Analyzes drawing view geometry and automatically adds common dimensions including
overall sizes, hole diameters, radii, and critical features. Accelerates drawing

tools.name: verify_model
tools.title: Verify Model
tools.description:
Check the active part or assembly against what you meant to build.

Call this as the last step of a build (and whenever a step looks
suspicious). A modelling tool returning success does not prove the
geometry is right; this reads the model back and compares it with
your expectations. Give only the expectations you know; each becomes
one check. With no expectations it just reports what it measured.

Units: mm, mm³ and kg. ``bounding_box_mm`` is the overall size
``[x, y, z]`` in model axes (a sketch on the Front Plane extrudes
along z). Widen ``relative_tolerance`` when your hand calculation
ignores fillets or chamfers, and ``length_tolerance_mm`` when
``measured.bounding_box_method`` is ``assembly_box`` (SolidWorks'
assembly box can be slightly larger than the parts). Mass depends on
the assigned material; without one SolidWorks uses a default density.

Each check reports ``expected``, ``actual``, ``tolerance`` and
``passed``: ``true``, ``false``, or ``null`` when the value could not
be measured (never counted as a pass). ``verdict`` is ``pass``,
``fail``, ``inconclusive`` (nothing failed, something unmeasured) or
``report_only``. ``status`` stays ``success`` when the model does not
match: the tool worked, the model is what failed.

anyOf.description:
Expectations for ``verify_model``; every field is optional.

Unknown fields are rejected so a misspelt expectation (``volume`` for
``volume_mm3``) fails loudly instead of silently not being checked.

mass_kg.description: Expected mass in kg (depends on the material)

bounding_box_mm.description: Expected overall size [x, y, z] in mm, in model axes

feature_count.description: Expected number of modelling features (extrudes, cuts, fillets, patterns...); sketches, the origin, folders and the three default planes are not counted

no_interference.description: true to require that no components overlap (assemblies)

relative_tolerance.description: Allowed relative error for mass and volume (0.01 = 1 %)

length_tolerance_mm.description: Allowed error per bounding-box axis, mm

input_data.description:
Expectations
and tolerances. Defaults to None (report only).

tools.name: discover_solidworks_docs
tools.title: Discover Solidworks Docs
tools.description:
Rebuild the SolidWorks API index on purpose. The lookups don't need it.

The lookup tools (lookup_api_method, lookup_api_interface,
find_related_api_members, search_solidworks_api_help) build the index
themselves on first use, so call this only to rebuild it, to read a
specific SolidWorks year, or to save a copy elsewhere. It reads every
interface in the installed SolidWorks type library (each member's
parameters, return type and description), plus the VBA library
references. SolidWorks must be installed, not running; it is never
started or called.

Returns ``summary`` (interface, method and property counts),
``type_library`` (version, year and .tlb path), ``year`` and
``output_file``, the saved index (megabytes, so it is not returned).
Fails with a message naming the installed years when ``year`` isn't
installed, or saying SolidWorks isn't installed here.

Example input: ``{"year": 2026}``

anyOf.description:
Input schema for ``discover_solidworks_docs``.

Attributes:
    output_dir (str | None): Folder to save the index in.
    include_vba (bool): Whether to scan for VBA library references.
    year (int | None): The SolidWorks year whose type library to read.

output_dir.description: Folder to save the index in; default .generated/docs-index. The lookups only read the default folder, so another folder is for keeping a copy (pass it back as index_file).

include_vba.description: Also list the VBA type libraries registered on this machine

year.description: SolidWorks year whose type library to read, e.g. 2026; an error if that year isn't installed. Unset: the year the server was started with (--year), else the newest installed.

input_data.description:
Year, output folder and
whether to include VBA references. Defaults to None.

tools.name: search_solidworks_api_help
tools.title: Search Solidworks Api Help
tools.description:
Search SolidWorks API interface and member names by keyword.

Use this when you don't know the exact name: "chamfer" finds
IFeatureManager.InsertFeatureChamfer. Then call lookup_api_method on
a match for its parameters and return type. Matches come from the
SolidWorks type library installed on this machine.

Setup: none. SolidWorks must be installed, not running; it is never
contacted. Nothing has to be called first: the first call builds the
index (about a second) and later calls reuse it. ``index_status`` is
``ready`` (saved index), ``rebuilt`` (built for this call) or
``unavailable`` (no index could be built; ``guidance`` says why).

Returns ``matches`` (interface, member, member_type, score),
``guidance``, and ``fallback_help`` suggesting MCP tools for the
task, with ``year`` and ``type_library_version`` of the library that
answered.

Example input: ``{"query": "chamfer", "max_results": 5}``

anyOf.description:
Input schema for ``search_solidworks_api_help``.

Attributes:
    query (str): Words to search member and interface names for.
    max_results (int): How many matches to return at most.
    auto_discover_if_missing (bool): Accepted for old callers; unused.

year.description: SolidWorks year whose API to answer for, e.g. 2026. Usually leave unset: the server's --year, else the newest installed. A year that isn't installed is explained in the result's note.

index_file.description: Path to a saved index JSON to answer from instead of the installed type library, e.g. one copied from another machine. Rarely needed.

query.description: Words to find in interface and member names, e.g. 'chamfer' or 'SelectByID2'

max_results.description: Maximum number of matches to return

auto_discover_if_missing.description: No longer needed: the index is built automatically when missing. Still accepted so existing callers keep working.

input_data.description:
The search words and
options. Defaults to None.

tools.name: lookup_api_method
tools.title: Lookup Api Method
tools.description:
Look up one SolidWorks API method or property: parameters, return type, description.

Use this before writing or debugging a SolidWorks API call (VBA, a
macro or COM) to check that the member exists on that interface and
how to call it. Answers come from the SolidWorks type library
installed on this machine, so they match the installed version.

Setup: none. SolidWorks must be installed, not running; it is never
contacted. Nothing has to be called first: the first lookup builds
the index (about a second) and later lookups reuse it.
``index_status`` is ``ready`` (saved index), ``rebuilt`` (built for
this call) or ``unavailable`` (no index could be built).

Names match regardless of case, as COM does. ``result.member`` is
SolidWorks' own spelling, with a ``note`` when yours differs. Each
parameter has a ``type`` and a ``direction``: ``in``, ``out``
(SolidWorks fills it) or ``in_out`` (pass a variable by reference).
``return_type`` is null when the method returns nothing; a property
has its value type there and an ``access``. ``result.found`` false
means there is no such member, and ``result.note`` says why,
including when no index could be built (SolidWorks isn't installed
here, or the requested year isn't).

Example input: ``{"interface": "ISldWorks", "method": "OpenDoc6"}``

anyOf.description:
Input schema for ``lookup_api_method``.

Attributes:
    interface (str): The COM interface the member is on.
    method (str): The method or property name.

year.description: SolidWorks year whose API to answer for, e.g. 2026. Usually leave unset: the server's --year, else the newest installed. A year that isn't installed is explained in the result's note.

index_file.description: Path to a saved index JSON to answer from instead of the installed type library, e.g. one copied from another machine. Rarely needed.

method.description: Method or property name, e.g. 'InsertFeatureChamfer'; case does not matter

input_data.description:
The interface and member
name. Defaults to None.

tools.name: lookup_api_interface
tools.title: Lookup Api Interface
tools.description:
List every method and property of a SolidWorks COM interface.

Use this to see what an interface offers, such as IFeatureManager,
or to check which interface a member is really on before calling it.
For one member's parameters, use lookup_api_method. Names match
regardless of case.

Setup: none. SolidWorks must be installed, not running; it is never
contacted. Nothing has to be called first: the first call builds the
index (about a second) and later calls reuse it. ``index_status`` is
``ready`` (saved index), ``rebuilt`` (built for this call) or
``unavailable`` (no index could be built).

Returns ``result`` with ``methods``, ``properties`` and their counts.
``result.found`` false means the interface isn't in the type library,
or no index could be built, in which case ``result.note`` says why.

Example input: ``{"interface": "IFeatureManager"}``

anyOf.description:
Input schema for ``lookup_api_interface``.

Attributes:
    interface (str): The COM interface whose members to list.

year.description: SolidWorks year whose API to answer for, e.g. 2026. Usually leave unset: the server's --year, else the newest installed. A year that isn't installed is explained in the result's note.

index_file.description: Path to a saved index JSON to answer from instead of the installed type library, e.g. one copied from another machine. Rarely needed.

interface.description: COM interface name, e.g. 'ISldWorks'; case does not matter

input_data.description:
The interface name.
Defaults to None.

tools.name: find_related_api_members
tools.title: Find Related Api Members
tools.description:
Find SolidWorks API members related to an interface or member name.

For an interface: its own members. For a member: the other members
of every interface that also has it (often used together), plus
members whose names contain it. Use it to explore around a call you
know, such as what sits beside InsertSketch.

Setup: none. SolidWorks must be installed, not running; it is never
contacted. Nothing has to be called first: the first call builds the
index (about a second) and later calls reuse it. ``index_status`` is
``ready`` (saved index), ``rebuilt`` (built for this call) or
``unavailable`` (no index could be built).

Returns ``result.related``: each member's interface, name, type and
why it is related. ``result.found`` false means nothing matched, or
no index could be built, in which case ``result.note`` says why.

Example input: ``{"name": "InsertSketch", "max_results": 10}``

anyOf.description:
Input schema for ``find_related_api_members``.

Attributes:
    name (str): An interface or member name to find relatives of.
    max_results (int): How many related members to return at most.

year.description: SolidWorks year whose API to answer for, e.g. 2026. Usually leave unset: the server's --year, else the newest installed. A year that isn't installed is explained in the result's note.

index_file.description: Path to a saved index JSON to answer from instead of the installed type library, e.g. one copied from another machine. Rarely needed.

name.description: An interface name (lists its members) or a member name (lists the members beside it), e.g. 'InsertSketch'

input_data.description:
The name and how many
results to return. Defaults to None.
